text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet said it would penalise with fines and extra taxes loss-making state enterprises for paying unjustifiably high wages in a bid to curb budget spending in line with IMF requirements.

-- Bulgaria's police said it had carried out checks on more than 30 hotels, restaurants and casinos at northeastern Black Sea holiday resorts in a bid to crack down on illegal gambling, corruption and organised crime in tourism.

-- Bulgaria may peg the lev this week as part of preparations to introduce a currency board system if the parliament approves a bill for the Bulgarian National Bank by Wednesday, Finance minister Muravei Radev said.
-- Bulgaria has exported timber worth some $19 million in the first quarter of this year, private Balkan news agency said.

-- Bulgaria may offer shares of its Telecommunication Company at the London Stock Exchange to evaluate the market price of the company ahead of its planned privitisation under an accord with the International Monetary Fund, Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov said.
-- Bulgaria's Sofia Municipal Bank said it had posted 3.1 billion lev gross profit by May 31.

-- Experts from the Economy Institute of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences proposed to peg the lev to the German mark as anchor currency in a currency board arrangement at a rate between 1,300 and 1,400.

-- Bulgaria's government approved the sale of a 70 percent stake of the Interpred World Trade Centre in Sofia to South Korean Daewoo Corp for $20 million, Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov said.

-- Journalists from Bulgaria's biggest 168 Chasa Pressgroup on Monday launched a one-hour protest against its owner Germany's publisher of the Westdeutsche Algemeine Zeitung with demands for 150 percent rise of their wages.
-- Bulgaria's state-owned Expressbank said it had posted 1.377 billion lev net profit for last year out of a 27.404 billion lev gross profit.
